data.headline: Your peers book plenty of meetings, but getting buyers to show up is the harder part
data.summary: Logistics companies with 201-500 employees get a median reply rate of 3.6% on cold email, and the middle half books between 3.6 and 10.6 meetings per 1000 emails. Show rates are where it slips: the median is 71%, and the bottom quarter sits at 60%. Deals that do start close in a median of 53 days. I would check show rate first, because every missed first meeting is one you already paid to book.

focus.why: The median peer gets 71% of booked meetings to happen, and the bottom quarter gets 60%. With 14 brokers each booking their own calls, a few points here adds up fast.

observations: Your team page lists 14 brokers who each book their own calls, so show rate depends on how each of them confirms a meeting.

takeaways.title: Booking meetings is not the bottleneck
takeaways.body: The middle half of your peers books between 3.6 and 10.6 meetings per 1000 emails. Plenty of those never happen, though: the median show rate is 71%.

takeaways.title: The meetings that happen are worth a lot
takeaways.body: Once a first meeting takes place, the median win rate on outbound deals is 22%, and the top quarter wins 32%. Every extra meeting that shows up feeds that number.

takeaways.title: 53 days is the middle of the pack
takeaways.body: Half of your peers close outbound deals within 53 days, and the slowest quarter takes 80 days or more. A deal past 80 days is worth a direct question about what is holding it.

next_steps: Pull last quarter's show rate for first meetings, per broker, and write the team number next to section 2.
Have the broker who booked each first meeting send a short confirmation the day before.
List the open deals older than 80 days and ask each owner what they are waiting on.
